White uses the pawn on c2 and the bishop on f1 to support d3; exchanging this support changes the central tension. Black's doubled e-pawns restrict one another; exchanges may free them, but the resulting open file can help either side. Other branches need a fresh assessment.

fields.description: Black offers the b-pawn in an Indian move order to build central space and active development.
fields.name: Blumenfeld Gambit
fields.strategy:
For the supplied reference position: White should improve minor-piece activity before launching a pawn attack; coordinated pieces can support a central break, whereas loose development allows the opponent to open the position with tempo. Black should complete development and secure the king: the f-pawn has advanced or been exchanged, so assess the resulting lines near the king before collecting another pawn.

Neither side should force an unsupported central break: establish piece support, then calculate which files open and whose king becomes exposed.

White's doubled b-pawns restrict one another; exchanges may free them, but the resulting open file can help either side. White's pawn on b5 controls a6 and c6; this can support flank play, but further advances spend time needed for central development.

fields.description: Duras Gambit: source-defined line Duras Gambit; moves 1. e4 f5 *
fields.name: Duras Gambit
fields.strategy:
For the supplied reference position: White should reinforce e4 against the opposing pawn on f5 while completing development and securing the king; extra expansion now risks losing the centre before the rooks can cooperate. Black should complete development and secure the king: the f-pawn has advanced or been exchanged, so assess the resulting lines near the king before collecting another pawn.

Neither side should force an unsupported central break: establish piece support, then calculate which files open and whose king becomes exposed.

White still has minor pieces on b1, c1 and f1 and g1; developing them gives the rooks more useful support than repeated moves by the queen. Other branches need a fresh assessment.
